title: Secrets Manager
summary: A secrets manager is a managed service for storing, controlling access to, and automatically rotating credentials such as database passwords, API keys, tokens, certificates and private keys, so that applications retrieve them at runtime instead of embedding them in code, images or configuration files. The service encrypts stored values with a key management service key, authorises retrieval with the platform identity system, versions every change, and can run scheduled rotation by invoking a function that creates a new credential and updates both the secret store and the target system. The security value comes from removing long-lived static secrets from build artefacts and repositories, from giving each workload a distinct credential that can be revoked individually, and from producing an audit trail of which identity read which secret and when. Practitioners must still address several hard problems. Workloads need a trustworthy identity to authenticate to the store, which in cloud environments usually means instance or workload identity rather than a bootstrap credential, otherwise the initial secret simply moves rather than disappearing. Caching matters because a rotated credential must not break running services, and rotation must be atomic enough that the old value stops working only after the new one is distributed. Also important are scoping read access so that one compromised workload cannot read every secret, detecting secrets that leak into repositories and images, and monitoring for unusual retrieval patterns.
objectives: You will be able to explain how runtime retrieval, versioning and automatic rotation remove static credentials from build artefacts.
You will be able to scope secret read access so a single compromised workload cannot reach unrelated credentials.
You will be able to design a rotation flow that avoids outages from caching and in-flight connections.
You will be able to use workload identity to authenticate to the store without a bootstrap secret.
You will be able to triage alerts on abnormal retrieval volume, cross-account reads and secret policy changes.
You will be able to respond to a leaked secret by rotating, revoking and confirming the old value no longer authenticates.
